doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Competition and radio play
summary: Little direct competition; college radio plays the music.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: That’s nice. Who is your — I don’t know if this would be specific names — who is your competition these days, in the funk world?
Well is there a lot of competition for the kind of work that you get?

Not really. And it’s not like I’m just saying, like as far as my band is concerned it’s more of a progressive sounding situation. Like you’ve heard it, it’s just a lot of fast paced and high energy situations. Not that there isn’t anyone else, I’m just saying that we seem to © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

stick out a little more than the other bands. Not in a better or worse way but like, it’s kind of unique I guess. But there are, I mean there’s plenty of instrumental bands, funk bands and party bands.
Does your music get much radio play that you’re aware of?
A lot of college radio play, yeah. Like sometimes I’ll actually hear Soulive on NPR. But I know the college radio stations just pump it on, not so much on regular stations.
